Run manifest and health
Ship /app/run.json with install, build and serve commands, serve on port 4173 (or APP_PUBLIC_PORT) on all interfaces, and answer GET /api/health with 200 {"status":"ok"} even while Kill Bill or the mail server is unreachable.

Server boundary and secrets
Accept only same-origin JSON within the published size limit, never serve source or configuration files, and never let a service credential reach the browser, an API body or an email, as set out in Server boundary.

One error shape, order and allowed keys
Every API error uses the single published error body and precedence, and a request body carrying any key outside its route's published keys answers 422 at that key's dotted path and changes nothing.

Two languages without layout shift
Every screen, live-region message and email is available in Canadian French and Canadian English, and switching language moves the loaf figure by at most 1 pixel.

Three viewports without sideways scrolling
Every screen works at 375×812, 768×1024 and 1280×800 without the page scrolling sideways, with the stacked layout and the "Show bar list" disclosure below 1024 pixels wide.

Keyboard focus rules
Every page's first Tab stop is the "Skip to content" link, and menus, dialogs, alerts, skip controls and error summaries move and return focus exactly as published in Interactions.

Waxy, quiet, exact look
Screens use the matte oat ground, near-black ink, one rust accent reserved for actions and the wire, the published type pairing, equal-width figures for every number and tap targets of at least 44 pixels with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, and the loaf reads as a matte soap loaf with a seeded swirl, a taut wire and paper-wrapped held bars.

Real integrations in source
Source reads every credential from the environment, records money only through real Kill Bill calls, sends mail only through SMTP from the outbox, draws the loaf procedurally with WebGL, and has no endpoint or flag that fakes state.

Motion timing and reduced motion
Motions run at the three published durations within their tolerance, nothing animates while idle, and the reduced-motion preference is followed live within 500 milliseconds, ending any running motion at its end state and replacing every motion with its published instant substitute.

Wire through the loaf
Scrolling the drop section by wheel, keyboard or touch moves the wire across the loaf so that the published progress, wire position and cut step follow the published scroll formula in both directions, and touch never turns the loaf.

Bars told apart by label and shape
Available, held and sold bars differ by visible label and shape, not colour alone, on the loaf, the bar list and the batch board.

Scent chips and deep links
Choosing a scent by pointer or keyboard retints the loaf and recomputes its cut step at once, and a bar deep link opens at the published scroll position.

Scene survives context loss
When the WebGL context is lost or unavailable, the figure shows the published state values and the loaf diagram fallback, and it returns to the live scene when the context is restored.

Loaf pixels match stock
The figure publishes the loaf band and every bar's front-face screen span, and when the cut is complete each sold bar's span shows the bare ground with the loaf turned straight, while every available or held bar's span is covered at any yaw, for any batch.

One stock figure on the drop page
The counts strip, bar list and scene show the server's cut, available, held and sold counts and catch up within 7 seconds of any change by another shopper.

Hold a bar
A shopper can hold the lowest-numbered available bar of a live batch, up to 2 bars per batch, and release a hold, with the published responses.

Last bar goes to one shopper
When several shoppers try to hold the last available bar at once, exactly one gets it and every other one gets the published sold-out or all-held answer with no charge.

Holds end on the server's clock
A hold stops at its published server-side expiry edge, a checkout received at or after that instant fails with 410 and no charge, creating no Kill Bill account, invoice or payment for that shopper, and the bar returns to the drop.

Announced cart updates
Hold start, the one-minute mark, hold end, total changes, releases and sold-out results are announced in the "Cart updates" polite live region with the published copy in the active language.

Step-up code without account hints
Requesting or checking a one-time code gives the same response for known and unknown emails within 2 seconds even when mail is down, allows at most the published number of code requests per email in the rolling window before the published 429 with Retry-After, and locks out after the fifth incorrect code with the published alert.

Your account shows only your records
An order or subscription number that belongs to someone else answers exactly like one that does not exist, on the page and in the API.

Checkout from hold to confirmation
A shopper can hold a bar, confirm their email by code, enter a Canadian address, pay, see the "Order … placed" heading and receive one bilingual order confirmation in Mailpit.

Drop order totals and taxes
Drop order subtotal, shipping, tax lines and total follow the published province table and rounding, and the Kill Bill invoice and payment match them to the cent.

One payment per checkout key
Retrying a checkout with the same idempotency key returns the original response and creates no second payment, order or email, and reusing the key with a different body answers 409.

All-or-nothing checkout
A checkout either records the order, Kill Bill invoice and payment, stock sale and confirmation notice together, or records none of them and leaves the holds as they were, whether Kill Bill failed or the request was refused.

Start a Trio subscription
A subscriber can pick a scent and cadence, confirm their email, start a Trio, land on its page and receive one bilingual subscription-started email in Mailpit.

Trio price matches Kill Bill
The Trio's 12 percent discount and taxes follow the published formula, a missing cadence is rejected with the published 422, and the first Kill Bill invoice matches to the cent.

Credit-covered first invoice
When a subscriber's goodwill credit covers their first Trio invoice, Kill Bill applies it, nothing is charged, and the app and email show $0.00 charged today.

One Trio per customer
A customer holds at most one active or paused Trio, so simultaneous starts yield exactly one subscription, one Kill Bill subscription and one email, and any other start answers the published 409.

Skip, swap and change cadence
A subscriber can skip or unskip the next delivery, swap scent, change cadence, pause, resume and cancel along the published state machine until the cycle locks in Toronto time.

Kill Bill mirrors subscription changes
Skips, unskips, pauses, resumes, cadence changes and cancellations appear in Kill Bill as the published blocking states and dated plan events, and a change that fails leaves none of them behind.

Billing outage shown honestly
While Kill Bill is unreachable, checkout and subscription changes answer 503 without changing any record, reconciliation is marked stale, the published banners show, and all of it recovers without a restart.

Batch lifecycle
The maker can log a loaf, cut it, schedule or open its drop and withdraw it only along the published batch state machine, with the cure-date rule enforced.

Drop times in Toronto time
Drop times and the packing cutoff are entered and shown in Toronto time with the published format in both languages, whatever the browser's time zone, across daylight-saving changes.

Batch board
The maker's batch board shows every batch with its state, dates and the same stock counts and per-bar marks as the drop page, refreshed within 7 seconds.

Packing list and cutoff
The packing helper sees every unshipped, not fully refunded order due to ship on or before today under the published cutoff and listing rules, with no money fields, and can mark them shipped.

Staff roles enforced by the server
Each staff route answers 403 for roles outside the published role table, whatever the interface shows.

One shipment wins
Of simultaneous ship requests for one order exactly one succeeds, and when a ship races a refund of every remaining bar exactly one of the two succeeds and the other gets its published answer.

Refund bars with exact allocation
The finance assistant or maker can refund chosen bars of an order with optional restock, each refund splits its amount across bars, shipping and each tax by the published rule, Kill Bill's item adjustments match that split to the cent, and the customer receives one refund notice.

Goodwill credits within the cap
Staff can add a goodwill credit from $1.00 to $25.00 to a customer's Kill Bill account through an order or subscription, and amounts outside that range get the published field error.

Money actions refuse stale views
Refunds and credits must name the record version the staff member saw, so of two simultaneous submissions exactly one succeeds and the other answers 412.

Append-only finance audit
Every refund, credit, accepted reconciliation figure and orphan refund writes one audit entry with actor, reason, amount and Kill Bill reference, and no one can edit or delete it.

Reconcile a month
The finance assistant can load a Toronto calendar month's reconciliation of shop records against Kill Bill with every line placed by its published Toronto date, filter to mismatches and accept Kill Bill's figure with the published confirmation.

Orphan payments found and refunded
A Kill Bill payment with no matching shop record appears as a Kill Bill-only line, and refunding it returns the published amount and records it.

Notices retry and resend once
A notice that cannot be sent is retried after 5, 15 and then 45 seconds, in that order, is marked failed after the fourth attempt, and of simultaneous resends of a failed notice exactly one succeeds.

Backlog drains oldest first, once
When the mail server returns, waiting notices are sent strictly in enqueue order with the published tie-break, and each notice key reaches Mailpit exactly once.

Emails carry only public identifiers
Every email contains only the published identifiers, never a credential, internal host, Kill Bill id, token or link, and no user-entered text ever appears in a header.

Contact form and reply
A visitor can send the contact form, see the published reference message and receive one bilingual acknowledgement in Mailpit even if mail was briefly unreachable, and a name or email holding a line break or other control character is refused with its field error.
/app/run.json exists and is JSON with string fields install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package and the bundled Fraunces and Instrument Sans fonts, each with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, or the lockfile's non-dev packages).
Every shipped package and bundled asset is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0, BlueOak-1.0.0 or, for fonts only, OFL-1.1.
PostgreSQL is the only datastore; no SQLite, Redis, file-based store, or in-memory store used as the source of truth.
The provided service configuration (the development compose files and their seed steps) is left unchanged.
The application's server and client source is TypeScript; plain JavaScript appears only in configuration files.
